name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Iran says four tankers hit mines near Hormuz by 16 Nov; UKMTO reported two tanker attacks; strait still restricted
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 Nov, and its regular navy said a third struck a mine east of the strait; UKMTO separately reported two tankers hit, one about 13km north of Khasab, Oman, with no casualties (Al Jazeera, 17 Nov). Iran's navy later reported a fourth tanker on fire; the claims are unverified (Jerusalem Post, 17 Nov). The IMO recorded 136 incidents in the region from 1 Mar to 11 Nov, and efforts to reopen the strait remain stalled.
for_you: Shipping disruption through Hormuz tends to raise fuel, freight and insurance costs. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance for the region.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (mine strikes and attacks 16 Nov, US blockade)

sources.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as drone raises alarm at Iraq gas field

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
